The game starts off very slow, but once you get past the first small hump of learning, it opens up into a massive world where you dictate what you want to do. Want to grind like in RuneScape? Go ahead. Want to build and farm? Go ahead. Want to PVP and fight humans instead of AI? Go ahead. Want to play it like a dungeon crawler? You can basically do that too. You get the gist, there’s just a lot of opportunity, which makes sense since it’s a sandbox.

The only negative I have is the camera view, you get used to it but not the biggest fan. personal preference

Albion is pretty nice MMORPG with vast crafting tree, a bit cartoonish graphic and classic point-to-action gameplay with isonometric camera view, set in fantasy-medieval times.
Developers introduced quite interesting mechanic of storage that would be bound to location, so it you're obsessed with collecting stuff (like I am) and want to move it to next town - prepare for long journey through all areas between as fary (ship transport) costs literally fortune.
Game offer solo- and team- instances and have solig Guild system with clan wars and semi-open-PvP.
Grinding is present and from the start you'd get two options - farm for mats and craft or buy stuff, from what I've been told by gmates - the tendency will continue through rest of the game.
There's ofc. ' P2W option ' (Premium), but fortunately you can farm silver and get it for in-game currency.

I had real fun playing it, but as the progress require commitment of time, and I'm too old for this sht. - I will not be playing it on a daily basis, just marking 'for later and moving on' ;)

It's not revolutionary in any means, but it have few cute mechanics and seem to be a solid title; that's why I'd recommend it for those who like that kind of games and can put a ' few ' good hours into it.

Albion Online is a sandbox mmorpg in which you get to write your own story, instead of following a laid out path. Explore a vast open world consisting of different unique biomes. Everything you do has an impact on the world, as in our player-driven economy every piece of equipment is crafted by players from resources gathered from players. The equipment you wear defines what you are. Switching from knight to magician is as easy as switching your armor and your weapon, or be a combination of the two. Venture out into the world or into dungeons and face Albion's inhabitants and wildlife. Go on expeditions to encounter even more challenges. Fight other players in open world clashes. Fight over territory, or city control in tactical group battles. Relax by retreating to your personal island. Build a home. Grow crops. Raise animals. Join a guild! Everything is more fun when you work together. Leave your mark in the world. In Albion, everybody that pays money matters.

As a veteran player of Albion Online from the early Beta days, I am confident to say that Albion Online is the best Full Loot PvP Sandbox game on the market. Albion stays true to the Sandbox term by having a completely player run economy, the freedom to choose your own path without class restrictions, and a deep and addicting progression system that progresses as you perform actions, rather than levels.

The game has changed a lot since the beta days but with the recent patch on March 20th 2019 called Oberon, the game implemented one of the best features yet in the "Random Dungeons". This, coupled with the Free to Play launch, have made Albion alive and well again. I highly recommend this game and don't get discouraged when you die for the first time.

Watch Twitch Streams and ask questions of the community and they will be happy to help you learn the game, survive, and thrive!

Albion Online não é um jogo, é um pesadelo virtual. Ele transforma cada segundo de tentativa de diversão em frustração pura, com grind interminável, mortes cruéis e PvP que parece projetado só pra te humilhar.

Por que é horrível:
• Morreu? Perdeu tudo, incluindo seu orgulho.
• Jogar solo é suicídio; sem clã ativo você não existe.
• PvP é sadismo puro, onde veteranos te esmagam antes de você reagir.
• Economia manipulada, cheia de monopólios e preços absurdos.
• Grind infinito para fabricar itens que você provavelmente vai perder na primeira batalha.
• Curva de aprendizado impossível, menus confusos e tutoriais quase inexistentes.
• Recompensas pequenas e facilmente destruídas por erros.

Resumo final:
Albion Online odeia você. Não é divertido, não é justo e não vale seu tempo. Se você gosta de sofrimento virtual, então… talvez você encontre um lar aqui.

DON'T BUY IF YOU ARE FROM EU. Even though the company is european, all the servers are located in USA. And they don't say it on their website. You will have worse ping than NA players and be at a disadvantage.

Developers lie that in this game the ping doesn't matter that much. But why locate it in USA rather than EU where the company is based if the ping doesn't matter? The fighting is like in MOBA's. With higher ping you will have problems dogging spell. Players and monsters teleport over the screen etc. This is a full loot on death game. Many EU players day because of a lag spikes, not their skill, and it is very annoying when you loose all your stuff because of a lag.

From what I've read, during beta some zones where on servers in NA, some in EU, so it was fair and balanced, but they changed it. Of corse it is harder to maintain, buy if they don't want servers in EU they shouldn't get EU money.

I also don't like Learning Points and focus per character which promotes creation of Alt characters, instead of playing and developing one.

Otherwise it is a fun game, but connection problems make it harder to be competitive in pvp for EU players.
